summary: Nine concrete, comment-endorsed tools, a book, and a launch tracker surfaced from 5,718 fully crawled comments.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Thingino
items.source_story_title: My security camera shipped a GitHub admin token in its login page
items.summary: Open firmware for supported IP cameras, with straightforward SD-card installation.
items.why_included: Two commenters provided concrete, successful installation and day-to-day-use reports.
items.evidence: One commenter upgraded two supported Sonoff cameras without issues, and another found the interface useful after an easy installation.

evidence_sources.author: makefu
evidence_sources.excerpt: The installation is straight forward if you choose a cam with SD-Card flashing support. I upgraded two of the Sonoff Slim Gen2 without any issues.

evidence_sources.author: jonah
evidence_sources.excerpt: I bought the cheapest PTZ camera they have listed and, as you say the install was easy. The interface is useful and it does what it says on the tin.

items.name: KDE Plasma
items.source_story_title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
items.summary: Linux desktop environment with configurable prevention of unwanted focus stealing.
items.why_included: A firsthand user called its focus-stealing control a favourite feature that works wonderfully.
items.evidence: A commenter specifically praised KDE Plasma's global focus-stealing setting and said they miss it on macOS and Windows.

evidence_sources.author: frameset
evidence_sources.excerpt: One of my absolute favourite features on KDE Plasma with Wayland is the global setting to control what can steal focus. It works wonderfully, and I always miss it when I have to use my work mac or windows computers.

items.name: AI Factory
items.source_story_title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
items.summary: An AI-assisted software-development process for taking products from early build to scale.
items.why_included: It was reported to materially improve code-agent-assisted development in a real workflow.
items.evidence: A commenter said their team found the process dramatically improved agent-assisted development when moving from 1 to 100.

evidence_sources.author: sharathr
evidence_sources.excerpt: we found that using a stable AI-SDLC process like: https://github.com/highflame-ai/ai-factory improves code agent assisted development dramatically specially when going from 1-100.

items.name: CachyOS
items.source_story_title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
items.summary: Performance-focused Arch Linux distribution with a KDE desktop option for gaming.
items.why_included: Two first-hand reports praised its smooth gaming support and usable out-of-box desktop.
items.evidence: One user reported six months with only one brief driver issue, while another said games needed minimal fussing and the desktop was strong out of the box.

evidence_sources.author: pixard
evidence_sources.excerpt: Hey may I suggest CachyOS + KDE? It’s very gaming oriented and you have a lot of great built in features. Everything just works.

evidence_sources.author: BoxOfRain
evidence_sources.excerpt: Another vote of confidence for CachyOS + KDE!

items.name: Ideogram 4
items.summary: Open-weight text-to-image model focused on layout, text rendering, and design work.
items.why_included: A practitioner running a high-traffic image-model site called it the best current open-weights option for text-to-image.
items.evidence: The commenter reported that Ideogram 4 outperformed Flux.2 in their prompt-adherence comparison and called it the best open-weights option for text-to-image.

evidence_sources.author: vunderba
evidence_sources.excerpt: Ideogram 4 is probably the best option

items.name: ComfyUI-KJNodes
items.summary: ComfyUI node collection that includes structured prompt-building support for image generation.
items.why_included: It was suggested as an out-of-the-box way to handle Ideogram 4's structured JSON prompts.
items.evidence: A commenter who uses a Qwen prompt preprocessor said the KJ prompt-builder node handles the required format out of the box.

evidence_sources.author: vunderba
evidence_sources.excerpt: I think that the KJ prompt builder node handles this out of the box in ComfyUI.

items.name: Brick
items.source_story_title: It's getting harder to focus every day
items.summary: A physical device that blocks selected distracting apps on a smartphone.
items.why_included: A recent purchaser gave an unusually strong direct recommendation for reducing social-media use.
items.evidence: A commenter said they could not recommend Brick enough for cutting back on social media.

evidence_sources.author: morelandjs
evidence_sources.excerpt: Unsolicited endorsement, but I bought a “Brick” device recently, and I can’t recommend it enough for cutting back on social media.

items.name: Next Spaceflight
items.source_story_title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on debut launch
items.summary: A website tracking upcoming rocket launches across providers and missions.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommended it as a neat way to see all upcoming launches.
items.evidence: A commenter said they had recently discovered the site and described it as showing all upcoming rocket launches.

evidence_sources.author: ck2
evidence_sources.excerpt: btw recently discovered this neat website that shows ALL upcoming rocket launches

items.name: When the Heavens Went on Sale
items.source_story_title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on debut launch
items.summary: Ashlee Vance's book about private companies reshaping launch and satellite infrastructure.
items.why_included: A commenter called it a great book for readers interested in private-space development.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended the book and noted that it profiles Astra, Firefly, Planet Labs, and Rocket Lab.

evidence_sources.author: josefresco
evidence_sources.excerpt: For those interested, just read a great book on this topic: When the Heavens Went on Sale by Ashlee Vance
